column1: # docs/dup-endpoints-behind-a-limit-2026-10-24.tsv ranks the pairs and says in
# its own header that it decides nothing, for a stated reason: the grouping key
# is host+path+QUERY, so the one thing it cannot see is a difference declared
# in OPTS rather than in the URL. canada-hydrometric-realtime / gc-hydrometric
# is the worked example - one collection, two limits, a deliberate pair whose
# difference lives in interval, record_type and page_resume.
# So this file reads the rows. For every pair it carries both sides' id,
# construct, interval, record_type, id_keys and limit value, and a verdict
# taken from the fields that decide the question rather than from the URL.
# THE ENTITY-TOKEN PROXY IS GONE. The cost classification in the other file had
# to guess pivot-vs-scheduled from a token in the URL, which is the same proxy
# registry_is_entity_pivot() leans on. Here the test is the row's own
# `interval`, which is the authoritative one. Measured on it:
#   RETIRE_GENERATED  47   a generated feed row (VJSON family) over one
#                          endpoint with an hpengine row - the IOC shape
#   PICK_ONE          33   two generated rows over one endpoint
#   READ_BOTH         13   two hpengine rows; this is the ONLY bucket where a
#                          deliberate pair can live, and it is 13, not 90
#   PIVOT_AND_FEED     0   measured on interval, not inferred from a token
#   UNRESOLVED        10   a side's URL sits in neither a `{ .id = ... }` block
#                          nor a V-macro call - a hand-written collector that
#                          builds its URL in code. Read by hand.
# WHAT "RETIRE_GENERATED" IS AND IS NOT. A generated row and an hpengine row on
# one endpoint is not a deliberate pair: VJSON carries no record_type and no
# id_keys AT ALL, so a differing record_type between the two sides is a
# property of the two CONSTRUCTS and says nothing about purpose. The first pass
# of this verdict read it as intent and called 62 pairs deliberate - most of
# them the exact shape already retired on this branch, a generated row
# shadowing a properly keyed hand-written one. The hpengine row is normally the
# keeper, for the reason ioc-sea-level-stations was: it declares an identity.
# TWO CONDITIONS BREAK THAT, and both are counted:
#   A. the SURVIVING hp row has no id_keys (8 pairs: CBS_NETHERLANDS_ODATA,
#      x2, safecast-radiation). Retiring the generated row there leaves ONE row
#      with no declared identity, which is rule 4b exposure and not a repair.
#      Key it, measure it, then retire.
#   B. the generated row asks the upstream for MORE records than the hp row
#      does (33 pairs - the whole BGS cluster at 200-300 against 100, the ODS
#      against 1,000). Harmless when the hp row pages, a real loss when it does
#      not, so the hp row's paging declaration is read before anything goes.
#   12 pairs have neither caveat: the generated row is the one to retire.
# NOTHING IS RETIRED ON THIS FILE. It is the per-pair read the other file asked
# for, not the repair. Every removal still wants what the IOC pair got: the
# endpoint measured, the candidate keys counted against distinct whole records,
# and the evidence written down before the row goes.
# HOW IT WAS MEASURED, and the defect found in the measuring. The resolver
# blanks comments to SPACES rather than deleting them so URL offsets stay
# valid, masks string-literal interiors for brace balancing (a `{q}` token in a
# URL otherwise breaks the block finder), and reads each V-macro's arguments
# off a table of its own `#define`. That last part is not decoration: the first
# version inferred the positions from the argument count - "if len(args) >= 12
# then IVAL is args[10]" - and there are TWO arities. The JSON family carries
# PATH and puts IVAL at 10; VRSS/VGEO/VCSV/VNCBI carry no PATH and put it at 9.
# So VGEO_IDKEYS would have had its DESCRIPTION read as its interval and every
# pair containing one would have reported a bogus "interval differs". That is
# rule 4c's defect - two readers of one declaration disagreeing - committed in
# a tool written to audit rule 4b. Fixing it took the resolved sides from 169
# of 206 to 191 and moved 22 pairs between buckets. The script warns by name
# when a V-macro has no signature entry or is called with an unexpected arity,
# so the next macro added to the tree cannot silently read as UNRESOLVED.
# Columns: the two sides are _a and _b; `kind` is the construct (a V-macro name
# or hp/struct), `lim` the value of the limit parameter this pair differs on.
